cards.text: The wall around Jerusalem is UP, friend. Nehemiah, the man who led the rebuild, is telling us what comes next in his own words. There's one last job to finish on those gates.

cards.question: The wall's done, but a gate doesn't do much if anybody can stroll right through it. What does Nehemiah set in place?
With the doors hung on Jerusalem's gates, the ___ are appointed, along with the singers and the Levites.

cards.text: Next, somebody has to run Jerusalem, and Nehemiah puts his own brother Hanani in charge. Making your brother the boss? BRAVE man.

cards.question: Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge of Jerusalem along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress. What reason does Nehemiah give for his choice?

answers.text: He was faithful and feared God more than most
He had fought off the enemies at the wall
He knew every family living in the city

cards.text: Then Nehemiah gives Hanani and Hananiah their orders for the gates. When it comes to this city, the man is taking ZERO chances.

cards.question: Nehemiah tells them to open the gates of Jerusalem at first light, as early as they can.

cards.text: Not until the sun is hot! Jerusalem's front gates just got a snooze button. And while the guards are on duty, the doors stay shut and securely fastened.

cards.question: Somebody has to keep watch over Jerusalem. Who does Nehemiah want appointed as the guards?

answers.text: Soldiers sent by the king of Persia
Hired men from the nearby towns

cards.text: Now step back and take a look at Jerusalem. The city is large and spacious, all wrapped up in that rebuilt wall.

cards.question: Jerusalem is large and spacious, but there are ___ people in it.
At least the houses inside Jerusalem's walls have all been rebuilt.

cards.text: Big city, houses not rebuilt, hardly anybody home. That's renting a whole stadium for your birthday and five people show up. Then Nehemiah says his God put something into his heart.

cards.question: God puts it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the nobles, the officials and the people, so they can be enrolled by ___.

cards.text: Then Nehemiah finds something. Me? I spent years in a junk drawer full of old receipts and takeout menus, and I never found ANYTHING useful.

cards.question: Right when Nehemiah wants the people enrolled by genealogy, what does he find?

answers.text: The register of those who first returned
A letter from the king of Persia
The scroll of the Law of Moses

cards.text: Here's what's in it: the people who came back to Jerusalem and Judah from captivity in Babylon, where Nebuchadnezzar, Babylon's king, had carried them off. Family by family and town by town, it lists them with their counts, plus the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants and descendants of Solomon's servants. Some families couldn't prove they came from Israel, and some priests couldn't find their family records, so those priests were kept out of the priesthood.

All told, the whole assembly is 42,360, plus servants, singers, horses, mules, camels and 6,720 donkeys. That's not a moving day, that's a TRAFFIC JAM. Then the governor, some heads of families and the rest of the people give gold, silver and priestly garments to the treasury for the project.

cards.question: In the end, all the Israelites move inside Jerusalem's walls to live.

cards.text: Everybody settles in their own towns, and by the seventh month the Israelites are home. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is NOT done.
